q: What do we know about feat-ae-depth-v2 in the app-engagement project?
a: feat-ae-depth-v2 is screens and features per active day, divided by a tenure-cohort baseline. It replaced depth v1 on 2026-02-04 after exp-504 showed v1 lifted the mean score of accounts under 90 days from 48 to 62.

q: What came of exp-503 in the app-engagement project?
a: exp-503 (10 percent randomised push holdout, Nov 2025, n = 214,000 accounts) found push sends added only +0.2 percent sessions over 28 days. That overturned the push-open correlation of 0.31 in fnd-ae-push-assoc, produced fnd-ae-push-null, and led to dec-ae-no-push-credit and the score v2 without push credit.

q: What does ae-attr-gbm-v1 in the app-engagement project depend on?
a: ae-attr-gbm-v1 scores 90-day attrition from feat-ae-active-days-v1 and feat-ae-depth-v2 plus tenure, with no push feature. Its label is ds-ae-attrition-labels, built from cards.churn_labels and app.sessions_daily.

q: What is the current engagement score in the app-engagement project?
a: ae-score-v2, which uses logistic-fitted weights on active days and depth v2 with no push credit. It supersedes ae-score-v1 and scores AUC 0.76 for 90-day attrition on holdout-2025q4 (n = 610,000).

q: What AUC does ae-attr-gbm-v1 reach on holdout-2025q4 in the app-engagement project, and with what n?
a: AUC 0.81 on holdout-2025q4, which has n = 610,000 active accounts from Oct to Dec 2025, measured in exp-506 on 2026-03-24.

q: Why did the app-engagement project stop giving the engagement score credit for push opens?
a: A randomised push holdout (exp-503, Nov 2025, n = 214,000 accounts) showed sends added only +0.2 percent sessions. The 0.31 correlation between push opens and the score in fnd-ae-push-assoc was reverse causation, so fnd-ae-push-null led to dec-ae-no-push-credit on 2026-01-30.
